mechanism: Beta-blockers impair the cellular uptake of potassium and reduce renal potassium excretion, increasing the risk of hyperkalemia when combined with potassium supplementation or high dietary intake.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels regularly; adjust potassium supplementation dosage or frequency; consider alternative antihypertensive if hyperkalemia develops or use ACE inhibitors/ARBs cautiously with this combination.
